findings.evidence: `grep -rn WeakDerivStep code` returns hits for `WeakDerivStepJetLp` only in W2p.lean:64 and W3p.lean:64; no file outside GraphStep.lean mentions `WeakDerivStep.prev`, `.deriv`, `.mk`, or `norm_prev_le`. Compare GraphStep.lean:236-239 with W3p.lean:131-134, and GraphStep.lean:280-284 with W3p.lean:214-217 / W2p.lean:196-199.
findings.fix: Make the order-specific spaces reducibly the generic one (`abbrev W3p ... := WeakDerivStep mu Omega p W2p.hessianL`, likewise `W2p` over `W1p.gradientL`) and define each order-specific name as a direct instantiation — e.g. `def W3p.thirdDerivativeL := WeakDerivStep.derivL _`, `theorem W3p.norm_thirdDerivative_le u := WeakDerivStep.norm_deriv_le _ u`, `theorem W3p.norm_sq_... := WeakDerivStep.norm_sq_eq_norm_prev_sq_add_norm_deriv_sq _ u`, and drop the duplicate `CompleteSpace` instances. If that is not wanted, delete the unused `WeakDerivStep` namespace instead of shipping a dead parallel API.
findings.issue: The whole `WeakDerivStep` lemma layer (`prevL`/`prev`/`prev_coe`, `derivL`/`deriv`/`deriv_coe`, `mk`, `prev_mk`, `deriv_mk`, `hasWeakFDerivOn_prev`, `norm_prev_le`, `norm_deriv_le`, `norm_sq_eq_norm_prev_sq_add_norm_deriv_sq`, the `CompleteSpace` instance, GraphStep.lean:194-288) has no user: grepping `WeakDerivStep` shows only `WeakDerivStepJetLp` and the two `mem_...` lemmas are consumed. `W3p` instead re-proves each of them with the identical script — W3p.lean:96-127 (`secondOrderL`/`secondOrder_coe`, `thirdDerivativeL`/`thirdDerivative_coe` vs `prevL`/`prev_coe`, `derivL`/`deriv_coe`), 131-150 (`W3p.mk`, `secondOrder_mk`, `thirdDerivative_mk` vs `mk`, `prev_mk`, `deriv_mk`, same `⟨WithLp.toLp 2 (u, T), (mem_..._iff_hasWeakFDerivOn _).mpr (by simpa)⟩` and `rw [..._coe]; simp [mk]`), 166-169 (vs `hasWeakFDerivOn_prev`), 187-217 (vs `norm_prev_le`/`norm_deriv_le`/`norm_sq_eq_...`), 234 (vs the `CompleteSpace` instance). `W2p.lean:98-199, 211` are the same duplicates, and W2p.lean:196-199 was rewritten in this PR into a byte-for-byte copy of GraphStep.lean:282-284. The claimed factoring therefore adds a second copy of the API rather than removing one.

findings.evidence: GraphStep.lean:109-117 (`by rfl` plus `rw [..., weakDerivStepSmulPairing, ...]`) and 155-158; the removed comments are visible in the diff hunk deleting W2p.lean's `weakHessianTestFunctional_apply` and `mem_w2pSubmodule_iff`.
findings.fix: Define `weakDerivStepSmulPairing` and `weakDerivStepTestFunctional` in term mode with the `Fact`/`HolderConjugate` instances supplied by `haveI`/instance arguments, and add a private `@[simp] theorem weakDerivStepTestFunctional_eq` stating the sum-of-pairings expansion; then replace the `rw [show ... by rfl]` with `simp only [weakDerivStepTestFunctional_eq, ContinuousLinearMap.add_apply, ContinuousLinearMap.comp_apply]`. At minimum restore both dropped comments explaining why the `show` is needed.
findings.issue: `rw [show weakDerivStepTestFunctional base phi v J = ... by rfl, weakDerivStepSmulPairing, ...]` bridges the goal to the two-`lpPairing` form purely by definitional unfolding of a tactic-mode `def` (`weakDerivStepTestFunctional`, line 82-93, whose body is elaborated under a locally introduced `Fact (1 <= conjExponent p)` instance), and then delta-unfolds a second tactic-mode `def` via `rw [weakDerivStepSmulPairing]`. The `rfl` holds only if the instances elaborated in the `def` and in the proof are definitionally identical — exactly the accidental-defeq reliance the rubric targets — and the comment the pre-PR W2p proof carried at this step (`-- Expose the private functional as the two lpPairings whose integral theorem applies.`) was dropped during the move. The same happens at line 155-158, where the `rw [show J ∈ ... ↔ ... ]` lost `-- Pass through the private kernel presentation once, keeping it out of the public statement.`

summary: The PR extracts a generic `WeakDerivStep` API but never uses its lemma layer: `W2p` and the new `W3p` re-prove every projection, constructor, norm bound and completeness proof verbatim, so the factored lemmas are dead and the duplicated scripts remain. The moved `weakDerivStepTestFunctional_apply` also keeps a `rw [show ... by rfl]` defeq bridge whose explanatory comment was dropped in the move.
